title: Automorphism schemes of proper algebraic spaces of dimension at most one
statement: Let $K$ be a field and $C$ a proper algebraic space over $K$ whose dimension is at most one [def-weil-field, def-trf-algebraic-space, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The functor on $K$-schemes $T\mapsto\operatorname{Aut}_T(C\times_KT)$ is represented by a separated group scheme $G$ of finite type over $K$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The representing bijections $G(T)\simeq\operatorname{Aut}_T(C\times_KT)$ preserve identity and composition and commute with every base change of the test scheme $T$, including nonreduced test schemes. Proper means separated, of finite type, and universally closed; for algebraic spaces, separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type (the local condition is tested on etale scheme charts), and universally closed means that every scheme base change induces a closed map on underlying spaces [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The fibre product is the fibre product of sheaves, agreeing with [def-pc-fibre-product] on schemes. No smoothness, connectedness, reducedness, projectivity, or stability hypothesis is imposed on $C$.

proof.text: Properness gives that $C/K$ is separated and locally of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-separated-space-dimension-one-scheme] to $C$ with its given topological dimension bound. Thus the given algebraic space is represented by a $K$-scheme, which we again call $C$. Under this representing isomorphism the structure morphism, diagonal and all base-change functors are the same; hence properness and the dimension bound are retained. In Lean, private helpers identify the points of the represented space with the scheme by a homeomorphism, reflect the closed diagonal through Yoneda, and transfer universal closedness using represented scheme pullback squares. These supply the precise scheme-level hypotheses without changing the algebraic-space definitions.

Apply [lem-sc-proper-dim-one-projective] to the proper scheme $C/K$. It supplies a closed immersion $C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_K$ for some $N\geq0$, so $C/K$ is projective. This theorem includes the empty scheme and does not assume reducedness or connectedness.

Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Every ideal of $K$ is either $(0)$ or $(1)$ and is generated by at most one element, so $K$ is Noetherian. The one-member affine cover $S$ therefore makes $S$ locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth].

The structure morphism $f:C\to S$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field]. Properness makes $f$ quasi-compact, separated and locally of finite type. Since $S$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $f$ locally of finite presentation. It is quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated], so it is of finite presentation by the definition [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Thus projectivity, flatness and finite presentation, all required by the Isom-graph theorem, hold for the original $C$.

proof.text: For every geometric point Spec Ω → Spec K, apply the already proved source-library theorem AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_pullback_le_of_field (WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.FieldBaseChangeDimension) to the locally finite-type representing scheme C/K. It gives dim(C ×_K Spec Ω) ≤ dim C ≤ 1 directly for the composite geometric-point map. This is the dimension-under-field-base-change argument of [lem-pc-dim-base-change]; no identification of the residue field with K and no dimension-extension normal-form theorem are needed. The bound includes the empty and zero-dimensional cases.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-curve-isom-graphs] with $X=Y=C$ and base $S$. It gives a separated $S$-scheme $G$ of finite presentation and bijections $\theta_T:G(T)\simeq\operatorname{Isom}_T(C_T,C_T)=\operatorname{Aut}_T(C_T)$, natural for every $S$-scheme $T$. Finite presentation includes quasi-compactness; locally its coordinate algebras are quotients of polynomial algebras in finitely many variables, hence are finitely generated. Thus $G/S$ is of finite type by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The graph theorem is a functorial statement on all schemes, so these bijections already apply to nonreduced $T$.

source.place: Tag 0DSQ (lemma-curves-diagonal-separated-fp), pulled back to (C,C); graph realization in the cited existing node

proof.text: Write $A(T)=\operatorname{Aut}_T(C_T)$. Pullback preserves composition and inverses: pulling back the equations $aa^{-1}=a^{-1}a=1$ yields the inverse equations, and composition is preserved by functoriality. Using $\theta$, identity, inversion and composition therefore give natural maps $h_S\to h_G$, $h_G\to h_G$ and $h_{G\times_S G}\to h_G$. Here $h_Z(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,Z)$ and $h_{G\times_S G}(T)=h_G(T)\times h_G(T)$ by the fibre-product universal property. By [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] these maps are uniquely induced by $e:S\to G$, $i:G\to G$ and $m:G\times_SG\to G$. Explicitly, if $u=\theta_G(\mathrm{id}_G)$, then $e=\theta_S^{-1}(1)$, $i=\theta_G^{-1}(u^{-1})$ and $m=\theta_{G\times_SG}^{-1}(p_1^*u\circ p_2^*u)$. Naturality gives $\theta_T(m(g,h))=\theta_T(g)\circ\theta_T(h)$, $\theta_T(i(g))=\theta_T(g)^{-1}$ and $\theta_T(e_T)=1$ for every $T$. The two associativity maps have the same value on every triple since $(a\circ b)\circ c=a\circ(b\circ c)$; the unit and inverse diagrams agree on every $T$ by $1a=a1=a$ and $a^{-1}a=aa^{-1}=1$. Faithfulness in the same Yoneda statement makes these equalities of scheme morphisms. Consequently $(G,m,i,e)$ is a group scheme as in [def-sc-group-scheme], and each $\theta_T$ preserves identity and composition. For any $v:T'\to T$, the graph theorem gives $\theta_{T'}(g\circ v)=v^*\theta_T(g)$; the composition formula remains valid after $v^*$, proving all requested base-change compatibilities. In Lean, identify the iterated slice over T with schemes over T.left, then use Yoneda and the explicit representation of the restriction by C ×_K T to obtain a multiplicative equivalence of automorphism groups. Its evaluation formula proves that the graph theorem's pullback commutation is exactly restriction by Over.map. The resulting GrpCat-valued presheaf is represented by G. Mathlib GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy constructs its group structure; the defining multiplication formula verifies that every representing equivalence is multiplicative, including with the larger universe of presheaf automorphisms.
